lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Colosse about the supremacy of Christ, warns against empty philosophy and rules, and calls believers raised with Christ to a new life (1:1-4:18).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Colossians and say who Paul says Christ is?
ev: Describe the main sections: the supremacy of Christ (1), warnings (2), the new life (3-4)

nodes.t: Thanksgiving, prayer and rescue into the kingdom
nodes.d: Paul gives thanks for the Colossians' faith, love and hope, prays that they will be filled with the knowledge of God's will and walk worthily, and thanks the Father who delivered us from the power of darkness into the kingdom of his Son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Colossians 1:13-14 says God has done for believers?
ev: Say what Paul prays for (1:9-11)
Say what the Father has done (1:12-14)

nodes.d: Paul says Christ is the image of the invisible God, firstborn of creation, by whom and for whom all things were created, head of the church and firstborn from the dead, in whom all fulness dwells and through whose cross God reconciles all things.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Colossians 1:15-20 says about who Christ is?
ev: List what Paul says Christ is and has done in 1:15-20
Explain how the Colossians were reconciled (1:21-22)
Say the condition stated in 1:23

nodes.t: Paul's ministry and the mystery: Christ in you
nodes.d: Paul rejoices in his sufferings for the church, says he is a minister to make known the mystery once hidden and now revealed, which is Christ in you the hope of glory, and that he labours to present everyone perfect in Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says the mystery is in Colossians 1:26-27?
ev: State the mystery of 1:27
Say what Paul does and why (1:28-29)

nodes.t: Rooted in Christ: complete in him
nodes.d: Paul says all the treasures of wisdom are hidden in Christ, warns against being taken captive by philosophy and the traditions of men, and says believers are complete in him, circumcised, buried and raised with him, forgiven, with the written record against them nailed to the cross.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why believers are complete in Christ, using Colossians 2:9-15?
ev: Say where wisdom and knowledge are found (2:3)
Say what Paul warns against (2:8)
Explain what God did with the record of debt (2:14)
Say what Christ did to the powers (2:15)

nodes.t: Shadow and substance: against rules and false humility
nodes.d: Paul tells the Colossians not to let anyone judge them about food, festivals or the sabbath, which are a shadow of things to come while the body belongs to Christ, and warns against false humility and man-made rules that cannot restrain the flesh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by saying these things are a shadow and the substance is of Christ (Colossians 2:16-17)?
ev: Say what the shadow and the body are (2:17)
Explain why rules like "touch not, taste not" fail (2:20-23)

nodes.t: Raised with Christ: seek things above
nodes.d: Paul says that because believers are raised with Christ they should seek and set their minds on things above, for their life is hid with Christ in God; they must put to death sins such as fornication and covetousness, and put off anger and lies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul tells believers to seek things above, using Colossians 3:1-4?
ev: Say what believers are to seek (3:1-2)
List sins to put off (3:5-9)
Say what is true in the new man (3:10-11)

nodes.t: Put on love: the new life in the church
nodes.d: Paul tells the elect of God to put on mercy, kindness, humility and patience, to forgive as Christ forgave, to put on love above all, to let the peace of God rule, the word of Christ dwell richly, and to do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Colossians 3:12-17 describes a Christian community?
ev: List what to put on (3:12-14)
Say how we forgive (3:13)
Quote the rule of 3:17

nodes.t: Households, prayer and walking in wisdom
nodes.d: Paul instructs wives, husbands, children, fathers, servants and masters, urges constant prayer, asks for prayer for opportunities to speak the mystery of Christ, and calls the Colossians to walk in wisdom toward outsiders with gracious speech.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Colossians 3:23 says about how we should work and for whom?
ev: Say what each household member is told (3:18-4:1)
Say what Paul asks the Colossians to pray for (4:3-4)
Describe how they should speak to outsiders (4:5-6)

nodes.d: Paul names Tychicus, Onesimus, Aristarchus, Mark, Epaphras, Luke and others, sends greetings to Laodicea, asks that the letter be read there too, and closes in his own hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of Paul's co-workers in Colossians 4 and say what Paul asks about the letter (4:16)?
ev: Name some of Paul's co-workers in 4:7-14
Say what is to be done with the letter (4:16)

nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.d: God creates the heavens and the earth, and all that fills them, in six days, and rests on the seventh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God made on each day, and what happened on the seventh?
ev: Retell what God made on each of the six days
Say that God rested on the seventh day and blessed it
